subject: TTFT + streaming SLO follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Sep 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT + streaming SLO follow-up

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about Acme's real-time personalization use case. Below is my read of the performance targets and next steps so we’re aligned. Please correct anything I’ve mis-captured.

Recap of requirements (from our conversation):
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target <= 200 ms for interactive personalization calls (90th percentile).
- Throughput: steady-state ~200 req/s, peak ~500 req/s (batching tolerable during peak windows).
- Concurrency: ~50 concurrent streams (bursts to 100 for short periods).
- Streaming: client expects streaming responses for partial personalization as they render UI — SSE preferred, WebSocket acceptable.
- Chunk cadence: ~50–150 ms between chunks; payloads are small (single-line text blocks, ~50–200 tokens).
- Fallback: acceptable to fallback to a slightly higher-latency model variant (TTFT <= 400 ms) for rare degraded conditions if we notify the client.

Questions / clarifications for your infra team:
1) Are you terminating SSE at CloudFront / CDN or at an internal proxy? (This affects connection lifetimes and idle timeouts.)
2) Is TLS termination handled at the edge? Any mTLS requirements?
3) Do you have per-connection/idle timeouts we should be aware of (CloudFront, ELB, proxies)?

What I’m proposing as next steps:
- I’ll send a short technical proposal (attached) with suggested SLO envelope, capacity sizing for Dedicated vs Hosted, and a measurement plan.
- Can we schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive next week with your infra/engineering (to cover SSE connection handling, chunk cadence verification, and a brief POC run)? I’m available Tue/Wed 10–2 PT.
- If you’re comfortable, please share a network diagram and any proxy/CDN config snippets — I’ll highlight any settings that could impact chunk cadence or streaming stability.

Attachments: redwood-ttft-sla-proposal.pdf (proposal & measurement plan)

Thanks — looking forward to continuing this.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform

Thanks Aditya — that summary looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- TTFT: our primary goal is < 250 ms at p90; we called out 200 ms as an aspirational bar for the most latency-sensitive flows. If you can demonstrate 200 ms in a POC that’d be ideal.
- Throughput/Concurrency: steady 200 rps, peak 500 rps. Concurrency typically ~50 active streams, can spike to ~100 for Black Friday-type events for short periods (~10–15 minutes).
- Streaming: SSE is our preference because it’s easier to integrate with our front-end stack, but WebSocket is OK if SSE proves unstable across our CDN.
- Chunk cadence: target ~100 ms between chunks, payloads small per chunk. We want smooth progressive rendering in UI.

Infra notes: we front with CloudFront, which terminates TLS at edge. Requests hit an internal ALB and then our app-proxy. We’ll attach a network diagram.

I attached the network-diagram.png. I’m happy to do the tech deep-dive — Tue 9/12 10am PT works.

Thanks,
Sam
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Commerce
sam.patel@acme-commerce.com

Sam —

Appreciate the detail and the diagram. Confirming next items from Redwood side:

- We’ll size an initial POC environment to demonstrate p90 TTFT of <= 200 ms for your core flow and validate chunk cadence at ~100 ms. We’ll include both Hosted and Dedicated sizing notes in the proposal so you can evaluate tradeoffs.
- For SSE over CloudFront: two things our infra team will validate in the deep-dive — edge idle timeout behavior and ALB/proxy keep-alive settings. If CloudFront truncates long-lived SSE connections, we’ll propose edge-friendly keep-alive patterns or a WebSocket fallback.
- Measurement plan: we’ll run synthetic tests from your region (us-west) with traffic profiles matching your steady and peak loads. We’ll capture p50/p90/p99 for TTFT, token throughput, and chunk cadence (ms between frames).

Questions for the tech deep-dive:
- Can your infra lead share ALB idle timeout and CloudFront origin configs?
- Do you use any synthetic monitoring currently that we can integrate to run identical tests?

I’ll update the attached proposal with an explicit SLO table and a POC checklist before the deep-dive. Looking forward to Tue 9/12 10am PT.

Best,
Aditya
